correctness.rationale: The history-reset model yields random-unitary CPTP fixed-time maps. Its coherence multiplier obeys the Volterra equation and Kummer solution; the specified trace distance equals the modulus of that multiplier. An exact Fraction-based 80-term rational certificate combined with an analytic bound on the entire omitted infinite tail proves D(3/r)<1/20 and D(4/r)>1/10. Trace-distance contractivity under positive trace-preserving propagators gives the nondivisibility result. The bound 0<=r A_(u/r)<=u gives a seven-Lipschitz difference estimate and an exact gap window, for arbitrary finite-dimensional Hamiltonians. A high-precision diagnostic was not used as proof.

value.rationale: The demonstrated positive physical Poisson hazard does not preclude operational information backflow in a history-dependent reset model. The result turns a nonlocal memory equation into an experimentally interpretable trace-distance witness with explicit nonzero lower bound, with a quantified 1/200-radius energy-gap band for arbitrary finite-dimensional Hamiltonians. Unlike numerical dip observations, the strict inequality is exactly certified; this is a motivated boundary between memory and operational non-Markovianity, without claiming a global classification.
